subject: Renewal proposal — anchor + sprint credits for Q4 capacity uplift

Subject: Renewal proposal — anchor + sprint credits for Q4 capacity uplift

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a refreshed renewal proposal that does three things:

- Locks current unit price for 12 months on a 20% committed uplift vs. current run rate (anchor).
- Provides a one-time sprint credit pool (200K token-credit equivalent) to help cover Q4 pilot spikes while they stabilize.
- Includes optional burst capacity at 1.5x for peak windows (billing on usage over committed).

I exported the ROI model you asked for — see NimbusMed_ROI_model.xlsx. High level asks from your side were: maintain per-token pricing, get guaranteed burst headroom, and a short-term credit to absorb onboarding spikes. This proposal aims to balance those with our margin targets.

If you’re comfortable with the structure, we can mark this as the commercial term sheet and I’ll route the term sheet to procurement for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Next steps: can you confirm internal approval to proceed with the 20% uplift commit number and accept the sprint credit band? If yes, I’ll loop Marissa and David to finalize the pricing math and legal redlines.

Thanks —
Rishi
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: NimbusMed_ROI_model.xlsx
From: Samir Patel <samir@NimbusMed.com>

Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — anchor + sprint credits for Q4 capacity uplift

Rishi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. High level this feels like the right shape. Two clarifying asks from procurement/team:

1) Can the sprint credit be structured as a true credit that offsets overage charges (not a marketing credit)? Procurement prefers line-item credits that hit invoices.
2) Can you hold the current per-token price for 18 months if we commit to the 20% uplift (we were hoping for a slightly longer price-hold given regulatory cert work and our forecasting uncertainty).

Also, what’s the minimum true-up cadence you’re open to? Monthly is preferred for us.

If you can make these adjustments, we can move quickly — likely a PO within two weeks.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform
NimbusMed

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal proposal — anchor + sprint credits for Q4 capacity uplift

Rishi — quick calc attached (I put a sensitivity table into the ROI workbook). Short answers:

- Converting the sprint credit to an invoice-offset credit is fine; it effectively shifts ~3.2% of expected year-one revenue to a contra line assuming full utilization of sprint credits.
- Extending the price-hold to 18 months on the 20% uplift increases downside exposure by ~4.5% relative to a 12-month hold under our long-run price forecast; acceptable with the following: we reserve right to limit burst pricing to a higher surcharge if hardware prices materially change (belt-and-suspenders language).
- Monthly true-up is operationally ok; finance prefers calendar-month cadence for invoicing ease.

I recommend: accept invoice-offset credit, approve 18-month hold, and cap sprint credit usage to production/pilot workloads only (no internal stress tests). I’ll mark these changes in redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf and send to Laura for legal review.

-M

Samir / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear asks. We’ve updated the term sheet to reflect:

1) Sprint credit reclassified as invoice-offset credit (appears as a line item on the invoice; applies before overage billing).
2) Price-hold extended to 18 months contingent on signed commit for 20% uplift (term sheet includes a limited force-majeure clause for market-driven pricing adjustments and an agreed surcharge band for burst overage).
3) Monthly calendar true-up for usage / true-up invoices.

I attached the redlined term sheet (redwood_term_sheet_v2.pdf). Once you confirm, Rishi will send the DocuSign envelope and we can accept a PO. Please note: the sprint credit is explicitly restricted to public production traffic (we call out test harness and adversarial testing as excluded).

If these terms work, please reply with approval and we’ll issue the DocuSign link.

Regards,
